why: Let k be the smallest global frequency. A subarray whose top frequency is exactly k is, in practice, the longest window where no user appears more than k times (the rarest user can always be included k times in the longest such window). "No count above k" is monotone, so a variable-size window with a frequency map finds it.
hints: First compute one number from the whole array: the minimum frequency over all users. What does a consistent window look like in terms of that number?
Every user in the window must appear at most k times. That condition survives shrinking, so for each right end you can keep the leftmost valid start and only move it rightward.
Counter for k, then slide: add userEvent[right]; while its window count exceeds k, drop userEvent[left] and advance left; track the best length. O(n).
pitfalls: k is the minimum over all users of their total count, computed on the whole array, not per window.
When the count of the incoming user exceeds k, only that user can be over the limit, so shrink until it is back to k.
IDs go up to 10^9: use a dict, not an array indexed by id.
